messages:
alejandra: Quick follow-up from the active/active RFC: we discovered an edge where region-hint fallback sends EU-resident writes to us-east when eu-west is saturated. Legal flagged this for PII tenants. We need to pick an operational mode for proxy behavior (deny / escrow / allow-with-audit) and an implementable control-plane contract.

mike: To add context, control plane attaches tenant.residency = 'eu' for a subset of customers. Proxy currently uses region_hint -> route -> fallback order. We can short-circuit fallback when residency is 'eu' but need to decide UX.

samir: My quick read: three tradeoffs
  * deny: simplest for compliance, lowest infra complexity, highest availability impact.
  * escrow/quarantine: accept at edge but keep data in EU-scoped escrow until mirror confirmed. Medium complexity, better availability.
  * allow+audit: route as today but create immutable audit events + alerting. Least infra work, worst compliance risk.

lucy: From SRE/ops: escrow means more regional storage + TTL eviction policies + clear operator signals for stuck entries. Deny means spikes of 403/409 for customers and support tickets. Allow+audit risks legal escalations if auditors find cross-border writes.

alejandra: Propose we model as explicit customer-facing residency_policy with three values: STRICT (deny), ESCROW (accept->escrow->mirror), PAWN (soft allow+audit). Control plane stores tenant.metadata.residency_policy. Proxy honors header X-Residence-Override for client opt-in on a per-request basis if tenant allows it.

mike: Implementation notes: proxy should return structured error codes. Examples:
  - 409.residency.strict_denied
  - 202.residency.escrow_queued;ticket=<id>
  - 200.residency.cross_region_audit=1
We should expose the ticket id so clients and audit logs can correlate.

samir: Escrow sketch: reuse the prewrite/raft-queue pattern but with region tag and tenant namespace. On enqueue write an escrow-tx record to EU-backed store with fields: tenant, key, payload-hash, enqueue_ts, ticket-id. Add auth-signed checkpoint so we can prove we received the request in EU. Mirror worker picks up when eu capacity normalizes. If mirror fails for TTL, escalate and surface to compliance.

nina: A question: how do we handle reads while an item is escrowed? We could return one of:
  - a read-denied response for strict semantics
  - the last committed value and a header X-Value-Staleness: pending
  - an explicit pending token clients can poll with ticket id
I prefer giving a stable last-committed value plus pending flag so UX isn't catastrophic.

lucy: Ops runbook snippet idea:
  - Alert rule: residency.fallback_ratio{region="eu-west"} > 0.01 for 5m -> page on-call + trigger pool prewarm.
  - Escrow watermark high: escrow.storage_bytes > 80% -> start-mitigation playbook (throttle soft-mode tenants, clear backlog exporters).
  - Stuck-ticket SLA: if any ticket > 48h -> Compliance pager and run a root-cause.

infra-bot: deploy: feature-flag 'residency_policy_v2' enabled for canary cluster on 2026-04-02 10:00 UTC (5% rollout).

mike: Control-plane API addendum (sketch):
  PATCH /v1/tenants/{t_id} { "residency_policy": "STRICT|ESCROW|PAWN" }
  Request header: X-Residence-Override: STRICT|ESCROW|PAWN (optional, only honored if tenant.policy_allows_override=true)
  Response: 200 + updated tenant object.
I'll open a PR with protobuf + proxy acceptance logic.

samir: For escrow we need two worker types: regional-escrow-writer (edge enqueue + signed audit entry) and escrow-mirror-worker (consumes when target region healthy). We should instrument escrow.queue_time_histogram, escrow.failures, escrow.mirror_lag_seconds.

nina: Read UX sketch: GET returns JSON with fields (value, residency_status) where residency_status in [committed, pending_escrow, denied]. Put ticket id in X-Residency-Ticket header when pending.

lucy: Dashboard panels: per-region fallback ratio, escrow queue length per-tenant tier, ticket age distribution. Add runbook play actions for each alert.

alejandra: Agreed next steps and owners:
  - Control-plane schema + API (mike)
  - Proxy enforcement + header semantics + error codes (mike)
  - Escrow design doc + worker prototypes + audit signing (samir)
  - Read-path contract + client error codes (nina)
  - Alerts/dashboards + SRE playbooks (lucy)
I'll write RFC addendum with examples (curl, error payloads) and a migration plan for existing tenants defaulting to PAWN.

mike: Timelines: I'll land api/proxy skeleton by EOD Friday. Flagging integration tests needed for denial path.

samir: I'll prototype escrow enqueue this week and wire the signed-audit log flow. Need to sync with security for signature scheme.

lucy: I'll draft runbook and create the Grafana dashboard template. Recommend we run the feature behind a flag for 4 weeks on canary before wider rollout.

alejandra: Thanks all. Tagging for follow-up: @mike @samir @lucy @nina. Putting this on my radar to convert into the RFC addendum tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
